# Reserved words, generated from the patterns in scope. Do not edit.
#
# Most of this is ADVICE now. A name may contain any of these words: a
# statement with two readings is an error that offers the bracketings, so
# nothing is refused at the declaration for what it might do to a reading.
# Using a word here still costs a bracket wherever the two meanings meet.
#
# Three sections are still rules, and say so: no name may BEGIN with the words
# of an anchor-only pattern; no complete name may also have a glued or pinned
# pattern's shape; and no pattern may use a word operator or injection word.
# Those competing name readings are not reachable by bracketing.
#
# A pattern below is written as it is declared, and «guillemets» mark the one
# thing that cannot be: a PINNED hole, which takes one word and has no
# declaration syntax yet. Everything outside them is ordinary source.

## COSTS A BRACKET INSIDE A NAME (0) — advice


## NO PATTERN MAY USE (2) — a word operator, everywhere, in every scope

    is           reads as an operator between two values, and no bracket tells the two apart
    otherwise    reads as an operator between two values, and no bracket tells the two apart

## COSTS NOTHING (8) — every hole before a word is determinate

    for each «one word, or a bracketed name» in (_)
    list of (_)
    lookup (_) => (_)
    old (_)
    optional (_)
    return
    return (_)
    stop

## NO NAME MAY BEGIN WITH (4) — a rule, not advice

    list of      from list of (_)
    old          from old (_)
    optional     from optional (_)
    return       from return (_)

## NO COMPLETE NAME MAY HAVE THE SHAPE (2) — a rule, not advice

    for each «one word, or a bracketed name» in (_)
    lookup (_) => (_)

## PROTECTED (2) — no pattern may use these as glue

    index        builds index of «a loop variable»
    of           builds index of «a loop variable»

## INJECTED (1) — names the compiler builds, and never asks anyone to rename

    index of «a loop variable»   a loop's counter
